rows.schedule: Second Schedule: Vessel Handling Charges
rows.section: A.1 Berth Occupancy Charge — All Vessels
rows.unit_label: US$ · First 24 hrs (or part) / Every subsequent 12 hrs (or part)
rows.section_notes: Vessels which spend 6 hours or less in Port enjoy a 50% rebate on Berth Occupancy Charge. | A vessel calling solely to load fresh water, bunkers, stores, or pick/disembark crew and spending 6 hours or less is granted 50% rebate. | A vessel occupying a commercial berth for reasons other than cargo works (e.g. breakdown, repairs, striking crew) attracts a surcharge of $5,000 per day of 24 hours or part thereof. | Exempted from Berth Occupancy: time spent on Christmas Day and Good Friday; a ship which fails to sail due to causes it is not responsible for (Harbour Master certified); ships berthing at the VALCO Berth at Tema.

rows.section_notes: Vessels which spend 6 hours or less in Port enjoy a 50% rebate on Berth Occupancy Charge. | A vessel calling solely to load fresh water, bunkers, stores, or pick/disembark crew and spending 6 hours or less is granted 50% rebate. | A vessel occupying a commercial berth for reasons other than cargo works (e.g. breakdown, repairs, striking crew) attracts a surcharge of $5,000 per day of 24 hours or part thereof. | Exempted from Berth Occupancy: time spent on Christmas Day and Good Friday; a ship which fails to sail due to causes it is not responsible for (Harbour Master certified); ships berthing at the VALCO Berth at Tema.

General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues is a charge for the use of the basic port infrastructure by vessels, cargo and passengers. The payment of Port Dues is to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues on cargoes shipped between Tema and Takoradi shall be charged once only, in the Port of Loading.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The following are exempted from Port Dues on Cargo: Mails, Goods landed in error, Passengers under 3 years of age, pets, vessels under 100 gross tons.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Light Dues is a charge for the use of Navigational Aids and related facilities by vessels. It is payable in the first Ghanaian Port of call by deep sea vessels and is exhausted once the vessel leaves Ghanaian waters. Vessels operating in coastal waters pay light dues per month, except small craft licensed as Supply/Support Vessels.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues and other charges incurred by a vessel as a result of a detention order by a Court, Government Agency or other Legal Authority shall be borne by the Ship's Agent or Owner.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues on Cargo shall be assessed on the weight or Cubic Measurement (CBM), whichever is higher, where the goods are not in containers.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues on Unpacked Vehicles shall be assessed on the basis of the category (Car, Mini, Utility, etc.) of the vehicle.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues on Transhipment Unpacked Vehicles are for both Inbound and Outbound and shall be charged against the Inbound vessel only.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues on Cargo in Containers shall be assessed on the basis of the length of the Container (20', 40', 45').

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port dues on Transhipment Containers are for Inbound movement only. Outbound movement shall be charged separately at the same rate.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Dues on Vessels shall be assessed on the gross tons (GT). Applicable exclusively to vessels which did not work cargo nor embark/disembark passengers, save vessels under the Ninth Schedule which pay Port Dues on both vessels and cargo.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Vessels discharging/loading on a “free-in” or “free-out” basis may be billed for Port Dues on Cargo: 50% in US dollars; 50% may be converted to Ghana Cedi at the ruling rate on payment date. Invoices are debited to the accredited agent.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Exempted from Light Dues: (a) Vessels of less than 100 GT; (b) Vessels calling for Bunkers, Ship's Stores, Fresh Water for use on board; (c) Vessels in distress or calling for emergency repairs; (d) Vessels calling for medical assistance for the crew.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Exempted from Vessel Dues: (a) Vessels of less than 100 GT; (b) Vessels in distress or calling for emergency repairs; (c) Vessels calling for medical assistance for the crew.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Vessel Handling Charges (Marine Charges) include Pilotage, Towage, Mooring/Unmooring, Shifting, Berth Occupancy, etc. and are to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The berthing of a vessel commences when the Pilot boards and ends when the first line is sent ashore to the bollard. Sailing starts when the first line is taken off the bollard and ends when the Pilot disembarks.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Normal pilotage uses one Pilot. Deployment of an additional pilot to assist normal vessel movement attracts 50% of the applicable Pilotage charge.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Shifting from one berth to another commences when the Pilot boards for the purpose of shifting and ends when the last line is fastened to the bollard. Shifting to the anchorage starts when the Pilot boards and ends when the Pilot disembarks.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Charges for Shifting are to the account of the vessel where the movement is at the Master's request or in pursuance of a Harbour Master's direction due to breach of a Port Regulation or performance standards.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Towage is compulsory for all vessels. One tug boat compulsory up to 10,000 GT and two tug boats above 10,000 GT. An extra tug boat attracts 50% Towage charge.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Vessels of 300m and above in LOA require a minimum of 3 tug boats for Towage.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Mooring/Unmooring charges apply to all vessels occupying a berth, buoy or mooring facility of the Authority, including private berths/wharves/anchorage/offshore facilities where Authority employees and craft are used.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Mooring/Unmooring operations include attendance to ropes and supply of necessary craft and Mooring Gangs/Crew.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Mooring/Unmooring charges apply to all vessels berthing alongside a quay, wharf, jetty, buoys or other mooring point, paid for each movement (Berthing, Sailing, Shifting, etc.).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Mooring/Unmooring at Offshore Locations (SPM, CBM, Oil Production Sites, etc.) attracts double the relevant rates.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The charge for Shifting of Vessels is inclusive of Towage, Pilotage and Mooring related to the movement.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Pilot Attendance is deployment of a Pilot for operations other than normal pilotage (e.g. Salvage, mid-stream and offshore cargo/survey operations).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Berth Occupancy Charge is assessed on the LOA range in metres as per Lloyd's Register of Shipping. It commences when the first line is sent ashore during berthing and ends when the last line is taken off the bollard when unberthing.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Pilotage is compulsory in all Pilotage Districts and shall be paid even if a Pilot is not deployed. All Supply/Support vessels moving in/out of the Sekondi Naval base must pay Pilotage to the Authority.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Pilotage, Towage, Mooring/Unmooring and Shifting charges are assessed on the GT range of the vessel/craft as per Lloyd's Register.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Pilotage, Towage and Mooring/Unmooring of a vessel not under steam (stalled/dead engine) or in distress attract double the relevant rates.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: For a vessel berthing successively at several berths during a call, the time from mooring at the first berth to unmooring at the last is one continuous berthing duration for Berth Occupancy.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: A vessel/craft using the anchorage at the request of the Authority (e.g. temporary unavailability of a berth, bad weather) is exempt from Anchorage Charges.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: A vessel intending to use the anchorage other than at the Authority's request must apply via the “Application to Use Anchorage” form ahead of arrival or within 12 hours of arrival. Failure attracts a fine of US$5,000.00 plus accrued charges. Vessels without an accredited local agent are denied use of the anchorage.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Authority permission must be sought before a private company provides under-water services in the Port. Failure to seek written approval attracts a penalty of US$10,000.00. Where a private company provides the service, it pays 25% of fees charged as Royalty to the Authority.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Where charges are assessed on weight, the higher of CBM or deadweight Tonne applies. A Tonne equals 1,000 kg or one cubic meter (CBM).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Where minimum charge does not apply, charges are calculated to the nearest Tonne (e.g. 5.2 tonnes → 5 tonnes; 5.5 tonnes → 6 tonnes).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Heavy lifts are charged using CBM or deadweight, whichever yields higher revenue. For conventional cargo, heavy lift rates apply where deadweight is used as the basis.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: For Oil and gas cargo, heavy lift rates (6–10t, above 10 up to 20t, and above 20t) apply where deadweight is the basis.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: If CBM is used as the basis for charging heavy lifts (per C3 and C4), the standard rate (lifts up to 5 tonnes) is used.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Cargo handling rates apply to normal working hours. Overtime attracts additional charges — assessed by cargo volume for stevedoring/ship-related shore operations, and by persons deployed × overtime hours for storage-related shore operations.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Where additional services are required, additional charges cover the reasonable cost of services provided.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Fertilizers (including in containers) shipped for agricultural purposes are exempt from the dangerous cargo rate and charged as non-hazardous (general) goods, including transit cargo.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Live animals shall be delivered/shipped per the direct route at all times. The receiver provides feed, water and other needs.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The cargo receiver/shipper supplies, at no cost to the Stevedore, the grabs, hoppers and other dry bulk handling equipment for loading/discharging Dry Bulk and Semi-Bulk cargoes.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: All heavy-duty equipment not normally plying public roads (metal-tracked, earth moving, mining dump trucks, pay loaders, crawlers, rollers, mobile cranes, compressors, asphalt machines, mobile generators, etc.) is treated as conventional cargo.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: All automobiles intended to carry goods/personnel that normally ply public roads (cars, vans, buses, agricultural tractors, construction dump trucks) are treated as Unpacked Vehicles.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Vehicles/Trailers in stacks of more than one, stuffed with other vehicles/trailers, attract rates per the vehicle/trailer type for the number in the stack.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Vehicles stuffed with personal effects or goods (other than vehicle accessories) attract one-half of the applicable rates.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Trailers stuffed with goods (e.g. knocked-down vehicle parts, machinery, tyres) attract one-half of the charge.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Vehicles stacked on trailers attract the appropriate charge for the vehicle type.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Vehicles/Trailers stuffed with knocked-down components or units of machinery/equipment are considered stuffed vehicles.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Articulated vehicles are charged as two units — a utility vehicle and a trailer unit.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Stevedorage, Craneage, Labour and Terminal Handling Charges of Transhipment Unpacked Vehicles are for both Inbound and Outbound, charged against the Inbound vessel only.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Dangerous Goods Group I shall not be stored in the Port — routed through direct mode at all times.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Transhipment containers with Dangerous Goods are routed through direct ship-to-ship mode at all times and not stored in the port.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The owner of a container RO-RO vessel carrying containers/project cargo must maintain appropriate cargo handling equipment on the ship for Licensed Stevedores; such use attracts no charge from the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Where such a vessel lacks appropriate equipment, Stevedores charge the ship at the Craneage rate for all containers moved across the ramp using their equipment.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Stevedores make no payments to the ship for use of ship equipment (cranes, derricks, lift trucks, tractor-trailer sets, gears, etc.), including equipment maintained on RO-RO vessels.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Stevedorage, Craneage, Labour and Terminal Handling Charges of Transhipment Containers are for Inbound only. Outbound movement charged separately at the same rate.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Transhipment Container volumes attract Rebate on Port Dues, Stevedorage and Terminal Handling Charges after attaining a throughput of 25,000 TEUs per annum, granted per the Rebate table.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
rows.description: The Authority and its Licensed Operators/Concessionaires reserve the right to assign a Quay Crane or Mobile Harbour Crane to expedite operations; such deployment attracts appropriate Craneage.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
rows.description: Craneage is in addition to the Stevedoring and Labour Overtime Charges. It is to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
rows.description: A minimum Craneage Charge applies when cargo volume during a ship call is low and total Craneage income is less than the minimum specified per crane.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: D. Assignment of Cranes and Craneage
rows.description: Craneage is only applicable when a crane is deployed as part of Stevedoring Operations.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Labour Charges cover Overtime, Stand-By, Idle Time and Extra Service for Ship Operations and Receipt & Delivery Operations.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Labour Charges for Ship Related Shore Activities (Overtime, Delay/Idle Time, Stand-by, Extra Service) apply to Imports, Exports, Transhipment and Transit, and are to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Labour Overtime for ship-related shore activities is determined by cargo nature and volume (tonnage/unit/TEU), applicable whether or not the vessel works during overtime hours.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Labour Delays/Idle Time/Standby hours in ship-related activities during overtime hours are logged and invoiced.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Labour Standby Charges (ship-related) are raised when labour is deployed during both normal duty and overtime hours on customer request.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Labour Charges for storage-related shore activities apply to both Receipt and Delivery of Cargo and to all trade categories; to the account of the Consignee.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Labour Overtime for storage-related activity is assessed on persons deployed (with prior agreement) and actual overtime hours; to the account of the Cargo Receiver/Consignee.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Overtime hours for stevedoring (incl. ship-related receipt/delivery): Mon–Fri Day Shift 1230–1400 and 1700–1930 GMT, Night Shift 0330–0730 GMT; Sat/Sun/Public Holiday Day 0730–1930, Night 1930–0730 GMT.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Overtime hours for Receipt & Delivery (storage-related): Mon–Sat Day 1530–1930, Night 0330–0730 GMT; Sun/Public Holiday Day 0730–1930, Night 1930–0730 GMT.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Cargoes shifted via quay or on board, and those landed in error by the stevedore, are exempt from Labour Overtime Charge.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Extra Service charge applies when labour is deployed for jobs ancillary to stevedoring (trimming dry bulk, salvage of damaged cargo, stuffing/unstuffing, cleaning hatches, laying dunnage). Based on actual men deployed.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: In Receipt & Delivery, Extra Service applies for ancillary shore activities (salvage, weighing, bagging spilled cargo, etc.).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: When labour is booked exclusively for extra service, the minimum chargeable time is 8 hours.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Preparation of Vehicle Condition Reports (VCRs) and vehicle-handling documentation is integral to handling and does not attract the Extra Service Charge.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Hire of Labour (Non-Stevedoring) applies to activities unrelated to traditional stevedoring/shore-handling. The hirer is responsible for deployment, supervision and any liability arising from the persons employed.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Terminal Handling, Storage and Transport charges on Empty Containers are to the account of the ship's agent.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The Terminal Handling Charge for Transhipment Containers is for one leg of the shipment.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The charge for Evacuation of Empty Containers does not include Lift-On-Lift-off Charge at the destination.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Storage rent on inbound containers/cargo (Imports, Transhipment Inbound, Transit Inbound) is computed from the date of completion of discharge to the date of delivery.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Storage rent on Export containers/cargo is computed from the date of receipt in the Port to the date of loading onto the carrying vessel.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Where a vessel's operation is disrupted (shifted to anchorage, equipment breakdown, dispute, etc.), storage rent days for discharged cargo commence from the last day of operation prior to the disruption.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: For import containers unstuffed in the Port/ICD, storage rent on the Empty Container is computed from the date it was unstuffed to the date of evacuation or shipment.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Cargoes consolidated for Export (incl. empty containers) but later removed from the Port attract full storage rent for the period spent, plus relevant Receipt & Delivery Charges, with no rent-free days.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Empty Containers imported to ship Export cargoes but later shipped as Empties enjoy a 7-day storage rent-free period.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Transit Containers attract no rebate on storage charges when empty and are invoiced as though they were Exports.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hiring of any plant/equipment commences from the time it leaves its station until its return; may be waived/modified under special circumstances (distance, duration, etc.).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hire of GPHA-owned Floating Craft or Cargo Handling Equipment is at the absolute discretion of GPHA, which may require additional insurance conditions.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Equipment hired out shall not be transferred by the Hirer to another party.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hire charges apply irrespective of whether the service is rendered during weekday, weekend, public holiday, day or night.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: “Within Port” (floating craft) = enclosed Harbour Basin and locations within the Anchorage Area; “Outside Port” = locations beyond the Anchorage Area. For cargo handling equipment in Tema, “Within Port” = area bordered by Meridian Road and the Tema Fishing Harbour Road; in Takoradi, within the port perimeter fence.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The equipment hire charge includes the operational and technical crew.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Minimum hire for floating craft: 2 hours (Within Enclosed Water Area), 3 hours (Within Anchorage Area), 4 hours (Beyond Anchorage – Offshore). A 2-hour charge is raised when a confirmed booking is cancelled before work begins.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Minimum hire for cargo handling equipment: 4 hours (Outside Port), 2 hours (Within Port). A 2-hour charge applies for cancelled confirmed bookings.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The hirer cannot transfer or sub-hire equipment to third parties without the owner's written consent.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The charge for hire of the Diving Pontoon includes the use of on-board equipment.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The charge for deployment of the underwater camera includes the Diver.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: For floating craft, the hiring period commences when the craft leaves its mooring and ceases when it returns. The charge is payable whether or not the purpose of hiring was effected.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hire of craft for salvage operations (towage of dead vessels, assisting vessels in distress, etc.) attracts double the Fifth Schedule rates. Also applies to Tug Boats assisting Floating Storage Units (FSUs) at midstream/anchorage/offshore.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The craft and appurtenances are presumed seaworthy when turned over, but the Authority does not warrant mechanical condition and accepts no responsibility for delays from any cause.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The Authority reserves the right to stop the operation of any craft to require repairs it deems necessary.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The hirer/user assumes sole responsibility and liability for injury/death or property damage arising from possession, use or operation of the craft, and shall indemnify the Authority, its officers and employees.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hire of fire-fighting equipment to any offshore facility attracts double the rates. Minimum hire: 2 hours Within Port, 4 hours Outside Port.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hire of Fire Fighting Equipment for vessel-related Stand-by/Attendance/Monitoring commences from berthing until sailing.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The cost of chemical used in fire-fighting is charged separately.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hire charges for floating craft and equipment apply irrespective of weekday, weekend, public holiday, day or night.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: All gears supplied are deemed in good order and returned in safe, clean, sound condition. Damaged gears are repaired/replaced by the Hirer.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: The number of pumps required for standing by or fire attendance is determined by the Fire Manager.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: G. Hiring of Floating Craft and Equipment
rows.description: Hire of Grabs, Container Spreaders and Cargo Handling Gears to a location outside the Port attracts double the scheduled rates.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: H. Licence Fees for Small Craft
rows.description: Licence Fees and Dues for Small Craft, Supply and Support Vessels are annual charges applying to individual licensed vessels/craft. The operator must be licensed as a “Small Vessel/Craft Operator”.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: A maximum of four packages not exceeding a total of 50 kg is exempt from charges. Excess baggage is chargeable per tariff.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The Authority is not liable for loss, mis-delivery, detention or damage to goods in transit areas, except where caused by want of reasonable foresight and care by the Authority or its servant. Independent contractors are not servants of the Authority.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Charges for logs and curls are payable by contracting agents on behalf of the owner, on the tonnage shown on the ship's manifest.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Storage rent on rejected logs is payable by contracting agents on behalf of the owner.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
rows.description: Goods shall not remain in a transit storage facility beyond 60 days (subject to Customs & Excise Regulations) from completion of discharge. Overstayed goods are moved to the State Warehouse/designated facilities; goods entered at Customs may be auctioned by Customs.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
rows.description: Any expenses incurred by the Authority in such removal or sales are a charge against the goods.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
rows.description: The Authority accepts no liability for loss, damage or deterioration of goods transferred to the State Warehouse, Government Warehouse, Back Sheds, Overstayed Container Terminals, etc.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: L. Removal of Goods Detained by Customs
rows.description: The Authority is not responsible for goods detained by Customs or other authorities for examination, testing, treatment, fumigation, destruction, etc. Expenses are a charge against the owner of the goods.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: M. Maximum Storage Period of Empty Containers
rows.description: The maximum storage period for any empty container is 90 days from date of receipt or the date it became empty. After 90 days, the container is impounded and legal procedures commence for disposal by auction to defray costs.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.section: N. Conversion of US Dollars to Ghana Cedis
rows.description: Unless otherwise specified, where agreement is approved to charge a US-dollar tariff in Ghana Cedi, the cedi charge is at the rate of exchange on the date of payment.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Any transhipment container whose contents are unstuffed or re-packaged in the Port loses the concessionary transhipment rates and is charged as Import for the inbound and Re-export for the outbound.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: It is the duty of the agent of the carrier/cargo to ensure the compressor and refrigeration system of a Reefer Container is in perfect working condition at all times. GPHA is not liable for any malfunctioning that might affect the condition of the content.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: The Agent of the carrier vessel is responsible for payment of all charges (electricity, handling, storage, etc.) that accrue on a Reefer Container not claimed or cleared, or whose contents are due for destruction by Customs, Port Health, etc.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Additional Handling of Container: handling not directly connected to loading, discharging, receiving or delivering (e.g. truck-to-truck transfer at consignee's instance; re-evacuation of short-shipped containers). Quay transfer during ship operation/stevedoring is excluded.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Additional Sorting: sorting of consignments/packages to consignees' marks, numbers, drop numbers, etc.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Bulk Carriers: vessels designed to carry dry bulk cargoes, including Container-Bulk Carriers (Con-Bulkers). Vessel Handling Charges apply irrespective of cargo carried.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Bulk-In-Bagged-Out (BIBO): an operation in which cargo arrives in bulk and is bagged at shipside. The shore operator transfers indirect-routed BIBO into storage.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Bulk Cargo — Grabbing/Conveyor: dry bulk cargoes loaded with grabs, hoppers, pneumatic or continuous handling systems.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Coastal Traffic: short sea shipping in Ghanaian/West African waters. National Coastal — cargo produced/imported and cleared for consumption in Ghana, shipped between Ghanaian ports on a licensed vessel (incl. recirculation empties). Intra-regional — cargo traded among ECOWAS countries. Regional Feeder — cargo carried inbound on deep sea vessels and transhipped from Ghanaian ports to other ECOWAS ports.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Containers: ISO and Non-ISO units; Flats, Platforms, Bolsters. 20ft = up to 20ft; 40ft = above 20ft up to 40ft; 45ft = above 45ft up to 53ft. 45ft and above 40ft are deemed 2.5 TEUs for billing. Excludes Skips, accommodation units, goose necks, ro-ro trailers and other wheeled units.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Direct Handling: continuous handling between ship and inland conveyance where cargo does not undergo intermediate transit storage.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Dangerous Goods (DGs): substances per SOLAS 1974 / IMDG Code and MARPOL Annexes. DG Group I = IMDG Classes 1 (Explosives), 2 (Flammable & Poisonous Gases), 5 (Oxidizing Substances & Organic Peroxides), 7 (Radioactive Substances). DG Group II = IMDG Classes 3, 4, 6, 8, 9. Container DG I = Classes 1,2,5,7 (direct route at all times). Container DG II = Classes 3,4,6,8,9 (limited time in Port). Mixed goods → charged as DG.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Direct Transhipment: handling/movement of cargo from inbound to outbound vessel at the same time, without intermediate storage.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Dirty Cargoes: cargoes that mess up/foul quay aprons, storage and operational areas during handling, or emit dust particles.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Dump Barge: a barge that is not self-propelled and is moved by a tug boat.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Exports: produce of Ghana for shipment to foreign markets (traditional and non-traditional commodities).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Failure to Report for Delivery: charge applicable to consignees/agents who fail to report after a container is scheduled and positioned for delivery.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Fire Attendance: response of fire tender and crew to fire incidents.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Fire Stand-by: deployment of fire equipment and crew to mitigate fire threats.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Fire Safety Dues: dues for the use of in-built fire suppression systems installed at Liquid Bulk Terminals.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Fire/Safety Monitoring and Supervision: deployment of fire equipment/crew to provide technical advice and supervise client operations.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: General Port Cleaning Dues: a general charge for cleaning the port, assessed against all dry bulk and dirty cargoes; to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Gross Tonnage (GT) of Vessel: measured per the International Convention of Tonnage Measurement of Ships (1969), effective 18 July 1994.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Indirect Handling: handling between ship and inland conveyance involving routing through transit storage.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Indirect Transhipment: handling/movement of cargo from inbound vessel into transit storage for later shipment on an outbound vessel.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Inland Clearance Depots (ICDs): terminals (Off Dock Terminals) licensed to provide Receipt, Delivery and Shipment Services for Containers and Vehicles (e.g. Safebond, Tema Container Terminal, TBT, TACOTEL, etc.).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: ICD Handling Charge: a charge for delivering inbound (import/transit-in) container to a consignee.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Inter-Terminal Transfer: movement of containers/vehicles/cargoes from one on-dock terminal to another. Transfer between two licensed ICDs uses the same rate as Terminal 1↔2.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: ISPS Dues: charge for implementing the International Ship and Port Security Code (SOLAS Ch. XI-2, in force July 2004); to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Layby Charges: applicable to Oil Rigs, Production Platforms and similar craft stemmed at mid-stream undergoing repairs/maintenance.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Length-Over-All (LOA): the length of a vessel in metres from extreme point forward to extreme point aft, as per Lloyd's Register.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Lift-On-Lift-Off of Container: relates to ICDs/Depot and involves loading a container from a truck where the customer provides the truck and the Terminal Operator provides equipment. Does not apply when THC is raised.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Lift-On/Lift-Off Operation: stevedoring using ship's cranes, derricks and quayside cranes. Vehicles/Trailers by Lo-Lo attract 25% surcharge above Ro-Ro stevedoring rates.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Light Dues: general charges for use of navigational aids; to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Oil Terminal Loading Arm Dues: a general charge for use of Loading Arms at the Oil Terminals; to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Opening of Containers: cutting security seals and opening for sighting or sampling only, without labour/equipment. If labour/equipment removes part of the content, Partial Unstuffing Charge applies.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Out of Gauge (OOG) Container: a container loaded above the top casting or beyond its length/width, requiring special spreader attachments or manual slings (flats, open tops stuffed above casting level, stuffed bolsters, damaged/warped/hogged containers, and those needing spreader extensions).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Over-Stayed Container Terminal: a GPHA-licensed facility for receipt, storage, auctioning and delivery of Overstayed Import Containers (containers designated for auction by Ghana Customs).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Partial Unstuffing Charge: for removal of part of a container's content for customs examination or security control; includes re-stuffing; in addition to the Terminal Handling Charge; to the account of the consignee/shipper.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Pipeline Dues: charges for use of pipelines connecting port terminals and tank farms (incl. the Tema Oil Refinery); to the account of the cargo owner.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Port Infrastructure Development Dues (PIDD): a special port due for financing future Port Infrastructure Development Projects, levied on all cargo and vessels; to the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Re-Circulation Empty Containers: empty containers that arrived as stuffed boxes and were later emptied (unstuffing into CFS, delivery to consignees, or shipment as break bulk).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Re-Exports: cargoes brought in under temporary arrangements (exhibition, samples, construction projects) shipped back to origin/third countries, or imports/transhipment re-packaged in the Port for shipment by sea. Charged as EXPORTS.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Restuffing Charge: packing cargoes that have been unstuffed (fully or partially) back into containers. Additional to the unstuffing charge (except partial unstuffing); to the account of the consignee/shipper.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Roll-On/Roll-Off (RO-RO) Operation: stevedoring operation on a Ro-Ro vessel.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Semi-Bulk [Grabbing]: use of grab/conveyors/continuous systems to load bulk cargoes emptied/bled from bags at shipside.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Semi-Bulk [Bleeding]: cutting open bagged cargoes and emptying contents as bulk at the shore or into cargo holds.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Stevedoring: handling/movement of cargo between the ship's hold and the storage area (and vice versa), incl. stacking/de-stacking. To the account of the ship.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Stuffing and Unstuffing Charge: removal of container contents or packing of cargoes into containers, separate from the Terminal Handling Charge; to the account of the consignee/shipper.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Support Staff: Terminal Clerks, Foremen, Supervisors, Plant Operators, etc.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: State Warehouse (SWH): a customs-bond warehouse for cargoes un-entered at Customs or unclaimed after 30 days of the carrying vessel's departure.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Terminal Handling Charge (THC): charge for delivering/receiving a container to/from a consignee/shipper or ICD, covering handling and movement between storage and delivery/receipt point. Applies to outbound containers, vehicles and general cargo; excludes packing/removal of contents. Empty container THC paid by the Shipping Line.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Transhipment: cargoes using Port facilities but destined for other countries, moving on the second leg by sea. Manifested as such on arrival. Except DG containers for TBT, transhipment cargo shall not leave the Port through landside gates. Unstuffed/re-packaged transhipment loses the rate and is charged as Import + Re-Export.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Transit Cargo: cargoes using Port facilities but destined for other countries, transported by inland modes (road, rail, inland waterway). Manifested/declared as such at arrival. Transit rates do not apply to empty containers.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Transport of Containers within Terminal: movement of containers within the same terminal; applicable to on-dock Terminal operations only.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Transfer of Containers/Unpacked Vehicles from Port to ICDs: movement of containers, vehicles and other cargoes from the Ports to any Licensed ICD.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Truck Waiting Fees: a charge for consignees/agents unable to process enough container loads to fill their trucks, where the partially loaded truck remains at the Delivery Bay awaiting a top-up.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Tonne: 1,000 kg or one cubic meter (CBM); the higher of weight or CBM is used to invoice. Iron and Steel Products (incl. steel pipes) are always invoiced using the higher of weight or CBM.

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Unitised Cargo: Palletised Cargo, Pre-Slung Cargo, Jumbo Bags and Paper Reels. Excludes Bundled and Coiled Cargo (steel, lumber, etc.).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Unpacked Vehicles: vehicles shipped on their wheels (Saloon cars, Mini Buses, Vans, Station Wagons, Cross Country Vehicles, Pickups, Tipper Trucks). Categories: Saloon/Estate (cabs up to 2t, up to 5 persons, incl. tri-cycles/aboboya); Mini (Mini Buses, Vans, Pick-ups, Cross Country, Station Wagons, above 2t up to 3t); Utility (Buses, Trucks, Road Tractors, Agricultural Tractors); Trailer Units; Driveable/Non-Driveable; Stuffed Vehicles; Machinery/Equipment (treated as conventional); Rollable Machinery; Devanned (Containerised) Vehicles (no THC after devanning, but attract Transfer and Storage at Unpacked Vehicle rates).

rows.schedule: General Terms and Conditions
rows.description: Charges are for implementing Annex I and V of the IMO MARPOL 73/78 Convention. Payable by all vessels calling at the Port save those exempt.
